source_review.notes: Checked current primary POSIX, Linux man-pages, Linux-kernel, and xv6 documentation for mutex types and ownership, robust recovery, semaphore waits and posts, semaphore scope, condition waits and clocks, futexes, kernel mutexes, completions, and RT mutexes. All 13 final cited URLs returned HTTP 200; a stale non-POSIX clock-page suffix was rejected before drafting.

evidence: Checked shared state S, invariant I(S), mutex M and owner O(M), condition CV, predicate P(S), capacity N, available C, claimed K, waiter W(CV), and live-user set U.
Reviewed ownership, count, predicate, completion, spurious wake, broadcast, robust recovery, timeout clock, cancellation, process sharing, and priority inheritance terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates exclusive responsibility, count conservation, condition truth, waiters, lifecycle, and terminal outcomes.

evidence: Executed the two-consumer model and confirmed an if-only path decrements one available item twice, ending at -1.
Confirmed loop-style recheck leaves count 0 and sends the second consumer back to waiting.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The sequential model assumes both consumers woke and serializes mutex reacquisition; it does not implement synchronization.

evidence: Re-derived semaphore conservation C+K=N with 0<=C<=N and exactly-once return for every claimed unit.
Checked condition protocol lock, while-not-predicate wait, atomic unlock-and-block, reacquire, and recheck across competition and spurious return.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The analysis keeps mutex ownership, semaphore capacity, condition predicates, and retained completion events semantically distinct.

evidence: Reviewed wrong-owner unlock, recursion, zero and maximum semaphore counts, overflow, double post, token leak, spurious and competing wake, heterogeneous predicates, wake-one and broadcast.

Reviewed timeout-publication races, wall-clock changes, cancellation after claim, owner death during journal update, repeated recovery crash, process exit and unmap, futex storage lifetime, priority chains, partial initialization, callbacks, close, restart, and destruction.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Ownership, conservation, predicate, timing, failure, recovery, priority, process-sharing, lifecycle, performance, security, and assurance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced named mutex invariants, semaphore conservation, paired condition mutexes, recheck, wake cardinality, robust repair, and quiescent destruction through ten examples and five answers.
Verified the executable counterexample exposes underflow while the guarded path preserves nonnegative count.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not conflate binary semaphore and mutex, notification and predicate, timeout and ownership resolution, robust detection and automatic repair, or futex and pthread semantics.

evidence: Reviewed state classification, invariant and ownership, predicate pairing, outcome enumeration, conservation, ordering and priority, admission closure, and adversarial validation.

Constructed counterexamples for non-owner mutex release, if-only condition wait, publish-after-signal, close with wake-one, canceled claimed token, owner-dead continuation without repair, and synchronization destruction with live waiters.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable synchronization obligations, not a formal proof of POSIX, glibc, Linux futexes, a kernel mutex, a recovery journal, or a real-time system.

evidence: Audited uses of atomic, exclusive, consistent, robust, recovered, available, correct, bounded, real-time, and certification.
Confirmed API guarantees, abstract conservation, toy arithmetic, application recovery, empirical latency, analytical blocking, security policy, and human assurance remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Robust owner-death notification is explicitly not presented as transaction rollback, and observed maxima are not timing bounds.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-023/report.json records if-final=-1, while-final=0, and second-consumer=waits for toy-condition-recheck under Python 3.

Reviewed acquisition, wait, hold, wake-to-run, herd, retry, timeout, cancellation, donation, throughput, topology, policy, clock, library, kernel, tracing, stress, owner-death, process-exit, and raw-result limitations.
